B. Using the Second Conditional to refer to hypothetical situations.
We use the second conditional when we are thinking about the present and imagining how it could be different given the condition.
People would be able to see better if we had a platform here. (We don't have a platform and people can't see.)
If we put up partitions, people would have more privacy.
It would be ideal if we had a t-shape room.
Quantifiers are words or phrases used to indicate the amount of, or quantity of something.
They come before the nouns they are modifying.
Example: We need a bit more space here for the catwalk.

You are going to choose a venue for a work event.
Go online and research different places/buildings that you could use to host the event.
Describe the place and use quantifiers. (There's enough room for 200 people.)
Talk about the negative aspects of each place, and imagine what could be different. (If we had more space here, we could have a DJ.)
Read your description to a friend.

Curator: As you can see, this is a grand hall with a number of possibilities.
Miranda: Indeed. I love the old stone. It's wonderful how they've kept the building's character while modernizing it. Look at all the frescoes on the wall!
Curator: Those were painted using the method of the late Renaissance.
Miranda: The glass ceiling over the dome is wonderful. It could be a cathedral!
Curator: The lofty space makes for wonderful concert acoustics.

Miranda: If we had a much smaller room, it would be perfect. What are the dimensions of the open area?
Curator: It's 150 by 130 meters. Of course it's hard to visualize while empty. The band could be positioned down there if you liked. We have a full-sized stage.
Miranda: I also need plenty of space for the reception. If there was a bit more space down the center for the catwalk, attendees could almost feel a part of the show.
Curator: If we had a t-shape, that would be ideal. People would be able to see well if you had a raised platform, just a little lower than the band, running the length of the stage.

Miranda: Are there any changing rooms?
Curator: There are lots of public restrooms which are rather small. However, there is enough space near the stage. It could be set up for the models to change. They would have privacy if you put up a few partitions.
